evidence: A coupled screen of the sky's food web, aerophytes' tenants and phosphorus on committed products: the coupled aerophyte model called live for representative bodies, the aerial, people, first-screen, taxonomy, surface-light, sky-ship and sky-fleet products, and from other branches the resources branch's phosphorus model and product, the provisioning branch's zonal-wind product and its ways-of-living product, bound by commit, blob and SHA-256. Tests check carbon and phosphorus closure in both states of the sky, that every edge bounds its quantity over every corner of its ranges, replacement of the dead against each body's surplus, the vertical response's physics against analytic limits, limits of the light and trim arithmetic, the exact reproduction of the resources branch's published case, conservation of the deposited flux, the wind code's time convention, every binding and exact regeneration. One read-only agent reviewed the study in three passes and recomputed its numbers independently; the fixes for its findings are in this product. No food web, population, tenant community, phosphorus cycle or trajectory is simulated, and no organism exists.

Third pass (the same agent, on the product 22c326c0 and symbioses c0bf1350): confirmed the second-pass fixes exactly (its own loop to 1e-16, 2^14 corners per body, state and case, the infeasible set, survival to size and the lightning scaling), reproduced Codex's consumer ledger, the symbioses product and the living-sail product, and found three physics corrections to the new timescale answer and five smaller points (third_pass_fixes).

Fourth pass (the same agent, a short confirmation on the product 18842b94 and symbioses 0e76bc25): confirmed the third-pass fixes, its own integration reproducing the overshoot (42.5-97.4%) and the bisected step share (0.406-0.504) to three decimals, and found one correction: the gas warms at fixed volume, so its heat capacity is rho c_v = (5/2) p/T, about 870 J/m^3/K, which shortens the thermal times by 1.4 to 0.2-20 hours; fixed.

review_fixes.finding: 1. The phosphorus in new tissue counted as kept aloft: falls of stock x hazard carried 1.8-7.2% of a reef's growth phosphorus, so the loops and the resources check treated growth as recycled.
review_fixes.fix: Two states of the sky throughout. Growing: every body spends its surplus on new bodies; their phosphorus (growth_p at the body's tissue mix; fermented gas at the low edge, photolytic at the high) is new stock, and the need is what leaves plus the change of stock. Mature: bodies hold their size, falls at the hazard are replaced, throughput is renewal plus replacement and the surplus beyond replacement pays for tenants. food_web gives growing, renewal and mature biomass; phosphorus.sky_loop takes the state; the falls table adds the falls a fixed cover would need at the growth rate.
review_fixes.effect: A reef with forest-floor pools recycles 92-97.5% mature and 76-92% growing (93-98% before); with the classes at their design shares the sky's need at 1% cover is 3.8-60 kt a year mature and 13-164 kt growing with forest-floor pools (4.3-54 kt before, reef only); a fixed cover with the whole surplus spent on growth needs 1,600-5,100 reef falls a year against 60-300 at the hazard.

review_fixes.finding: 2. The eaten base counted the regenerated-cellulose envelope as food, while long-lived bodies' structure went to litter.
review_fixes.fix: Edible carbon is the living tissue alone; the eaten bodies' envelopes go to the decomposers with the litter (eaten_offer shed_c); construction shares recorded (gas, tissue, envelope, construction respiration, starch store).
review_fixes.effect: Edible share of construction 5.0-8.1% (27-33% before); edible production at 8-15 m 0.077-0.094 kg C/m2 a year (0.39-0.50), 0.34-0.42 of a long-lived body's renewed green tissue ("twice" before).

review_fixes.finding: 3. The grazers' phosphorus-limited share (23-40%) came from pairing every range at the same end, which pulls two ways; the host's sugar was assimilated at the leaf-eaters' 30-50%.
review_fixes.fix: stoichiometry.edge_parameters pairs poor food, poor assimilation and phosphorus-rich consumers at the low edge (and the reverse), so the edges bound production; p_limit_corners gives the share and the subsidy over all 64 corners; sugar is assimilated at 0.9, a design guess.
review_fixes.effect: Carbon limit 20-45 g C per m2 of reef a year (7.1-28); phosphorus limit 7.9-41% of it at the edges and 3.7-89% over the corners, median 18%; the subsidy to reach the carbon limit 0.41-0.70 g P (0.03-1.6 over the corners; 0.14-0.41 before).

review_fixes.finding: 4. The 7.9% grazing share is of whole above-ground production but was applied to green tissue.
review_fixes.fix: Long-lived bodies' grazed share is 12-19% of foliar production (Metcalfe et al. 2014); Cebrian (2004) and Cyr & Pace (1993) stay as context.
review_fixes.effect: Grazing costs a reef module 3.8-6.0% of its surplus (2.5-5.7%) and a 1-km giant 7.6-12% (5.0-11%); the sky at 1% feeds 1.8-4.8 million albatross-scale grazers (1.2-4.5 million).

review_fixes.finding: 5. Sudden loads drew on reserves the aerophyte study already assigns: the spare superpressure is the day's water swing's allowance and the dumpable water is the damage reserve.
review_fixes.fix: Sudden loads stated as upper bounds, free in full only at the low point of the day's swing, with dropping water spending the damage reserve (capacity_rows docstring, reading rule, notes; headline key hundred_metre_sudden_upper_bounds_t).
review_fixes.effect: Numbers unchanged (a 100-m body takes at most 1.9 t at once by trim and 33 t dropping water).

review_fixes.finding: 6. "Biomass" included the 0.1 kg C/m2 a year of sugar the host gives its tenants.
review_fixes.fix: Biomass production excludes the sugar everywhere; the sugar is reported beside it.
review_fixes.effect: At 1% cover and the reference light, 162-413 Mt C a year growing and 134-397 Mt mature, with 38 Mt of sugar besides (200-451 Mt before).

review_fixes.finding: 7. The resources check divided tissue phosphorus by production that included phosphorus-free sugar, while the resources and aerial models' 1,000 g C/m2 is all dry biomass.
review_fixes.fix: The check runs on the biomass basis, per state, case and edge: the loop's throughput over the loop's biomass carbon. The formula's r is the loop's recycling taken onto the unharvested 95% of the throughput (equivalent_recycling), so (1 - h)(1 - r)F equals the loop's own non-harvest need exactly.
review_fixes.effect: Throughput 4.7-14.5% of Redfield's mature and 4.3-12% growing (3.2-10.4%); the published 10,726 t becomes 0.5-85 kt (designed pools), 8.3-104 kt (forest-floor pools) and 137-737 kt (nothing catches the litter) in a mature sky, and 22-251, 29-264 and 140-689 kt growing (0-45, 4.3-62 and 64-448 kt before).

review_fixes.finding: 8. The loop without pools counted the harvest twice and lost no grazer phosphorus; frass mixed carbon and phosphorus assimilation.
review_fixes.fix: Harvest leaves before shedding; frass is what the grazers eat less what they build; what remains aloft (renewal less harvest and departing tenants) is recycled or falls, so without pools the frass, the grazers' remains and the structure all fall.
review_fixes.effect: A mature reef recycles 45-68% alone (51-77% before).

review_fixes.finding: 9. Polar occupancy concentrations used the wind product's area shares rounded to four decimals.
review_fixes.fix: Exact band areas from the latitude edges (band_areas), in the occupancy and the deposition.
review_fixes.effect: 80-90 N at 10 km 3.4 times (3.6); at 20 km 12.0 (12.7) over the north pole and 8.6 (9.1) over the south.

review_fixes.finding: 10. The Sun's track was half a step off: the wind code centres output n at (n + 1/2) intervals. The snapshots of the routes also swing with the Sun's place.
review_fixes.fix: subsolar_longitude adds half a track step; the value used is the band-weighted land fraction (each band's time spread over its longitudes), with the snapshots kept as a check.
review_fixes.effect: Land share 75% at 10 km and 71% at 20 km (77% and 72% before); snapshots 77% and 72%, single snapshots 59-92% and 49-85%.

review_fixes.finding: 11. The light at 10 km took the ground's downward light, 7-11% low, and the day's mean gave its zero-light end points full weight.
review_fixes.fix: tenants.height_factor carries the ground spectra up by two-stream adding, (1 - A R)/(1 - R) for the layer below, direct and diffuse alike; the Sun is sampled at the midpoints of 91 steps.
review_fixes.effect: Level-top daylight 980-1,018 umol/m2/s over ground of albedo 0.05-0.2 and 1,112 over cloud (879-925 and 1,041 before); zone shares move by about 0.004.

review_fixes.finding: 12. The FMR extrapolation's cross-check was weak: the allometric 39 times must lie between the similarity terms, and Nagy's 30-170% spread was not carried.
review_fixes.fix: The flyer rows record the similarity bounds and the notes call the agreement a consistency check; flyers_fed carries the spread.
review_fixes.effect: 1.1-16 million albatross-scale grazers at 1% over the spread, beside 1.8-4.8 million at the allometry.

review_fixes.fix: Each corrected: the aerial study's 1,000 g C/m2 sits at the top of the giants' and reefs' ranges; the two-stream law matches the product to a median 0.0035 at 400-560 nm, within 0.01 in 79% of bins and up to 0.068 off in absorption; the forest-floor ranges by class; the floor of falls and departing flyers given for the reef; the small body's cost partitioned with its construction respiration; the albatross-scale grazers as 23-62% of Earth's wild birds; the routes' release spacing in latitude and hour; the gathering medians as a series; the rounding (91-94%, 0.43-0.53, 0.21-0.45%, 0.14-0.84); the north pole's gathering at 10 km; a spore's 210 days from 10 km; the falls docstring; deposition and falls with the same class shares; the fall speed through the sky-ship density profile; the wind product's cell read from it; the sky fleet's gliders read and tested against the glide ratios; the checks.json link.
review_fixes.effect: Litter drifts 6-12 km from 10 km and 41-81 km from 20 km along the wind and at most 20 km across it (6-12 and 42-84 km before); forest-floor litter phosphorus 3.9-10 kt a year class-weighted (4.8-16 kt reef only).

review_fixes.finding: 14. Tests that checked less than the notes said.
review_fixes.fix: Route positions against the half-step frame; the two-stream law at every bin; hemispheric and longitude-split atlases; sky totals against the aerial product's area; similarity with the people product's own spans; occupancy against exact areas; edges bounding every corner; loop closure in both states; the glide ratios within the sky fleet's gliders.

review_fixes_note: First-pass findings and fixes, with their effects on the product of 10:18 (ec61d2ec). The second pass's harvest fix moved some of those effects; second_pass_fixes gives the present values.

second_pass_fixes.finding: 1. The harvest share was paired at the end that does not bound the need: people return 99% of harvested phosphorus, so more harvest lowers the need wherever the sky keeps less than that of what it sheds, yet the high-need edge took the high harvest.
second_pass_fixes.fix: phosphorus.loop_terms takes explicit values and edge_values the edges; sky_loop evaluates both harvest shares and takes the one that bounds the need at each edge, recording it (designed pools, which keep 99.9%, take the high harvest at the high edge). test_edges_bound_the_need_over_every_corner enumerates 16,384 corners per body, state and case, with the grazers' P built consistently at each corner.
second_pass_fixes.effect: Class-weighted need at 1% cover with nothing to catch the litter 62-424 kt mature and 71-528 kt growing (67-382 and 76-486 before); with forest-floor pools 3.5-61 kt and 13-165 kt (3.8-60 and 13-164); designed pools unchanged at 0.26-50 and 9.4-154 kt. A mature reef alone recycles 38-70% (45-68%). The resources check with nothing to catch the litter 125-827 kt mature and 130-749 growing (137-737 and 140-689), with forest-floor pools 7.0-108 and 28-267 kt (8.3-104 and 29-264).

second_pass_fixes.finding: 2. The mature sky was never checked for feasibility: replacing the dead costs the hazard times each body's whole construction carbon, gas included, and at the high hazard with fermented gas that exceeds the surplus of 500-m and 1-km round giants and 150-m modules.
second_pass_fixes.fix: food_web.replacement gives replacement, surplus left, its share and the net growth of the cover for every body, light, gas route and hazard; mature figures appear only where the surplus pays for replacement; food_web.feasibility lists every row and the infeasible ones; food_web.demography sets the hazard against the aerophyte product's growth times (survival to size) and its lightning; falls rows and mature loops carry the flags.
second_pass_fixes.effect: Replacement takes 1-24% of a lesser body's surplus at the reference light, 9-66% of a round giant's with photolytic gas and 22-162% fermented, and 1-51% of a reef module's (4-142% fermented). Infeasible: fermented 500-m (110%) and 1-km (162%) round giants and 150-m modules (142%) at hazard 0.005 and GPP 2. Mature biomass ranges unchanged, as the photolytic rows set them. 1-km round giants reach full size at 31-80% at the low hazard and 0.3-32% at the high; 2-km reefs at 58-92% and 7-66%. A 2-km body is struck 0.003-0.007 times a year under the Moon's mean storms.

second_pass_fixes.finding: 3. Small items: the light gain at 10 km quoted as 6-10% (6% is the cloud case); the envelope as 19-28% (18.8-27.5%); the growing sky's resources rows labelled new stock as downward export; the lesser class used the 100-m body for the need and the 150-m body for falls.
second_pass_fixes.fix: 9-10% over ground of albedo 0.05-0.2 and 6% over cloud; 19-27%; the resources rows split the formula's total into new_stock_aloft_kg and downward_export_kg; the falls take the 100-m body.
second_pass_fixes.effect: With forest-floor pools a growing sky's formula total is 22-195 kt of new stock and 8-74 kt to the ground and away; 100-m falls: 9,700-48,300 a year at 1% cover, 0.016-0.048 t of P each, 0.5-6.2 g/m^2.

second_pass_fixes.finding: 4. The author asked "How sudden is sudden? 0.63 - 2.1 tonnes across what timescale?", and the tables carried no timescale.
second_pass_fixes.fix: tenants.vertical_response and response_table: the static sink of a fixed-volume body, the superpressure it takes, the buoyancy period with added mass, drag damping, settling, venting and dropping times, and a reef module's load shared through a 2-km raft; tenants.md "How sudden is sudden" answers in prose.
second_pass_fixes.effect: Period 25 minutes for any lone body and 67-102 minutes for a 2-km raft; sink 190 m (63 m for 100-Pa modules). The third pass corrected the step and venting figures (third_pass_fixes).

third_pass_fixes.finding: 1. Venting within minutes is adiabatic and costs 1.4 times the trim rule's superpressure, so fast venting does not turn a step into a gradual load.
third_pass_fixes.fix: vent_at_once_share_of_trim = 1/gamma with vent_at_once_s; the notes say venting takes 71% of the equivalent at once and the rest as the gas warms, while dropping water costs no superpressure.
third_pass_fixes.effect: "A body that vents within a tenth of its period meets a step as if it were gradual" became "venting within minutes takes 71% of the equivalent at once; dropping water takes all of it".

third_pass_fixes.finding: 2. The 1.24 factor and the 81% gradual share hold the gas at its own temperature; as it warms to the lower air the cost falls back toward the trim rule's.
third_pass_fixes.fix: superpressure_used_warmed_pa with the sky-ship lapse and with the lapse the density profile implies; passive_gradual_share_warmed; gas_thermal_time_s from the contents' heat capacity at fixed volume, rho c_v = (5/2) p/T, and an exchange of 2-10 W/m^2/K (a design range).
third_pass_fixes.effect: A gradual load over hours is taken passively up to 94-100% of the trim equivalent (81% over half an hour); the gas warms over 0.2-20 hours.

third_pass_fixes.finding: 3. The equivalent-linear overshoot understated strongly damped small bodies.
third_pass_fixes.fix: tenants.step_peak_sink integrates the nonlinear float with quadratic drag (fourth-order Runge-Kutta to the first turning point); passive_step_share_of_trim bisects on the integrated peak.
third_pass_fixes.effect: Overshoot 42-97% of the sink (25-98% before); peak 1.4-2.0 times the sink; a passive step survives 41-50% of the trim equivalent (41-65% before); a step needs 1.6-2.0 times the margin of a gradual load.

third_pass_fixes.finding: 4. The demography quotes left out the product's 4-mol/mol fermentation rows.
third_pass_fixes.fix: food_web.demography uses the food web's two gas routes, photolysis and 2.1 mol/mol fermentation.
third_pass_fixes.effect: The quoted 76-545, 38-126 and 234-702 years and their survivals are exact on those routes.

third_pass_fixes.finding: 5. The raft's added mass treats a porous raft as a solid disc.
third_pass_fixes.fix: Stated as an upper bound in the code and the notes; the raft's period is "up to" 67-102 minutes.
The mature forest-floor need 0.008-0.13 g; the Quetzalcoatlus-scale count 33,000-1.5 million.

third_pass_fixes.finding: 7. The resources check inherited the loop's harvest choice, which bounds the loop's need but not the formula's own term.
third_pass_fixes.fix: resources_check takes, at each edge, the harvest share that bounds the formula's need.
third_pass_fixes.effect: Designed pools, mature, low edge 0.44 kt (0.50); growing designed pools low edge 21.9 kt (22.0).

third_pass_fixes.finding: 8. Codex's unallocated assimilate is credited nowhere and its size was not given.
third_pass_fixes.fix: food_web.md gives it: 18-26 g C per m^2 a year on a reef module, 59-92% of level 2's carbon potential, 7-10 Mt C a year at 1% cover, outside the sky snow's carbon; its fate stays open.

not_performed: A population model: the counts of flyers and grazers are energy and phosphorus budgets, and how the sky divides between growing and mature bodies is open
Trajectories with sailing, storms and steering; the routes are the passive long-run routes in 3-day mean winds
Measured tissues: phosphorus contents, resorption and turnover of designed aerophyte tissue are design guesses

The vertical response takes a rigid fixed-volume body, a solid-disc raft and design ranges for drag, valves, drains and the envelope's heat exchange; no landing impact, tie compliance or control law is modelled

Primary reading of Cyr & Pace 1993 (medians through Burghardt & Schmitz 2015), Cleveland et al. 2013 (abstract and results excerpts), Sugden & Robins 1979 (as cited by later bromeliad studies), Golley 1968 (through van der Meer 2021) and Phlips et al. 1986 (cited for its subject); several precedents rest on abstracts, as sources.json records
The atlas grid is an ignored input on the research drive; without it the land share falls back to the water scenario's
Atlas and climate-model longitudes are taken to share their zero meridian
